frequency_question: How often do highly contested, high-impact agency rules successfully survive administrative and structural friction to reach final publication within a tight presidential term window?
membership_rule: Includes economically significant final rules published by executive agencies that faced intense legal opposition and procedural hurdles; excludes routine, non-contested technical adjustments.

cases.name: EPA Clean Power Plan Repeal / Replacement
EPA Mercury and Air Toxics Reconsideration
EPA Waters of the United States (WOTUS) Repeal

provenance_note: claimed 7 hits but 6 of 12 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 12 named major contested rules across recent administrations; believed to represent a fair sample of highly friction-prone regulatory attempts.
known_gaps: Excludes minor rules and rules that were quietly dropped before formal challenge.
skeleton: Total major highly-contested agency rules tracked through the administrative pipeline divided by those that successfully reached final publication before facing fatal structural blocks.
multiplier: 7 hits out of 12 named high-friction major rules = 58.3%
validity_reason: Base rate tied to the current administrative law regime and judicial review standards, which remain stable through the current presidential term.
